footer.tagline: Care routing for every Indian home: what care, how urgent, and who should go.
footer.team: Built by team OCTUPUS · KIET Group of Institutions
footer.event: HackIIITD 2026 · CAI, IIIT-Delhi · AI for Healthcare Access
footer.disclaimer: CareCompass helps route care. It does not diagnose, prescribe or replace a doctor. In an emergency, call 112.
footer.dpdp: Privacy: requests are processed only to route care. Nothing is sold or used for advertising, in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. This demo uses synthetic data only.
footer.sourcesNote: Synthetic dev data (ours) · KTAS triage · Disease-Symptom · Symptoms-to-Diseases (Kaggle)

paramedic_home_visit.name: Paramedic home visit
paramedic_home_visit.short: A paramedic comes to your home
paramedic_home_visit.meaning: A trained paramedic visits to check vital signs, dress minor wounds and assess common illness.
paramedic_home_visit.when: Fever or cough in an elderly person, minor falls or sprains, BP or sugar checks for someone who cannot travel.

nurse_home_visit.name: Nurse home visit
nurse_home_visit.short: A nurse comes to your home
nurse_home_visit.meaning: A nurse provides ongoing care at home: injections, drips, wound or catheter care.
nurse_home_visit.when: Injections or drips the doctor advised, dressing after surgery, bedridden patients, newborn care.

gp_teleconsult.name: Doctor on phone / video
gp_teleconsult.meaning: A general doctor talks to you on a phone or video call.
gp_teleconsult.when: Mild, common problems like a cold, mild fever in an adult, acidity, a rash, or questions about a report.

specialist_referral.name: Specialist appointment
specialist_referral.meaning: An appointment with a doctor who focuses on one area, such as bones, skin, eyes or the heart.
specialist_referral.when: Problems lasting weeks or months, or that need a specific expert: joint pain, vision, sugar control, pregnancy check-ups.

emergency_referral.name: Emergency help
emergency_referral.meaning: This needs an ambulance or emergency care immediately.
emergency_referral.when: Chest pain, severe breathing trouble, unconsciousness, seizures, stroke signs, heavy bleeding and other danger signs.

home.eyebrow: For families caring for loved ones
home.title: Describe the problem in your words. We find the right care.
home.subtitle: Speak or type in English, Hindi or Hinglish. CareCompass tells you what kind of care fits, how urgent it is, and which caregiver nearby should go, and why.
home.demoUser: Papa ko do din se bukhar hai aur khansi bhi
home.demoReason: Fever with cough for 2 days, no breathing difficulty reported.
home.demoMatch: Hindi-speaking paramedic, 3 km away, free at 4 pm
home.threeSub: Every request is turned into a clear decision you can act on, with the reason shown.
home.q1d: Paramedic, nurse, doctor on call, specialist, or emergency, matched to what you describe.
home.q2d: Routine, same day, or immediate. When in doubt, we choose the safer, more urgent option.
home.q3d: The best caregiver near you by skill, distance, free time, language and rating.
home.careTitle: Five kinds of care, explained simply
home.careSub: You do not need to know medical terms. Here is what each option means.
home.safetyTitle: A safety gate that works even if the AI fails
home.safetySub: Before any model runs, and again after, a rule-based check looks for danger signs in all three languages. If one is found, we skip everything else and show you how to call for help.
home.safety1d: Chest pain, breathing trouble, unconsciousness, stroke signs, seizures, heavy bleeding, poisoning and more, in English, Hindi and Hinglish.
home.safety2d: "Saans ki dikkat nahi hai" means no breathing problem. Negations are handled so that you are not sent to an emergency by mistake.
home.safety3d: We only route you to the right care. No disease names, no medicines. A doctor decides treatment.
home.safety4d: If anything goes wrong, or the AI is slow, a local model and the rules still give a careful answer.
home.builtTitle: Built for everyone in the family
home.built1d: Tap the mic and talk. Answers are read aloud.
home.built2d: Write the way you speak, with any spelling.
home.built3d: Bigger text and high-contrast mode in one tap.
home.built4d: Follow-up questions come with simple buttons like Haan / Nahi.
home.ctaSub: It takes less than a minute.

how.title: How CareCompass works
how.subtitle: From a voice note in Hinglish to a booked caregiver, with a safety gate at both ends.

flow.intakeD: Only if it changes the decision, max 4
flow.triageD: LLM + local model, the more urgent wins
flow.pathwaysD: Eight symptom categories (fever, cough, breathing, chest pain, headache or dizziness, abdominal pain, vomiting or loose motions, urine problems) are graded S0–S3 from danger signs, readings and who the patient is. S3 goes straight to emergency.

layers.name: Interface
layers.desc: Responsive web app with voice input, read-aloud, Hindi/English UI, large text and high contrast.

layers.name: API
layers.desc: Stateless FastAPI service: POST /api/v1/triage with the full conversation each turn, plus booking and caregiver endpoints.

layers.name: Safety
layers.desc: Deterministic red-flag engine with negation handling, run before and after every model.

layers.name: Understanding
layers.desc: Language detection, Hinglish normalisation, slot extraction and a follow-up policy that asks only when it matters.

layers.name: Decision
layers.desc: TF-IDF model, fine-tuned MuRIL and a hosted LLM with retrieved examples, combined with asymmetric safety; then caregiver ranking.

how.dataSub: Only synthetic data and cited public datasets. Never real patient data.

choices.name: Under-triage is the worst error
choices.desc: Low emergency threshold, rules that override models, and the more urgent label wins on disagreement.

choices.name: Fewer questions
choices.desc: A follow-up is asked only when a missing detail could change the decision. Most requests need none.

choices.name: Every decision explained
choices.desc: Plain-language reasoning tied to the user's own words, and a reason for every caregiver match.

choices.name: Fast and robust
choices.desc: Around 10 ms without the LLM; every LLM call has a 6-second timeout and a local fallback.

how.layersSub: From what you see on screen down to the decision engine. Safety sits in the middle and wraps every model.
how.pathwaysSub: The five most common complaints are graded the way a senior doctor would: danger signs first, then how long and how high, what else is happening, and who the patient is. Thresholds were set by our clinical mentor from WHO, NICE and Indian national programme guidance.
how.ladderNote: Every pathway runs, and the most severe one leads. Babies under 3 months, young children with a danger sign, people 65+, pregnancy and long-term conditions move a case up. Missing information never moves it down.

pathwayList.name: Fever
pathwayList.asks: Danger signs, how many days, thermometer reading, then follow-ups on headache, cough, body pain, stomach or chills
pathwayList.example: Platelets 80,000 + stomach pain → S2, same-day doctor and a home blood test

pathwayList.name: Cough
pathwayList.asks: Breathing at rest, blood (streaks or a spoonful), how long, wheeze, TB contact
pathwayList.example: Cough for 3 weeks with night sweats → S2, formal TB test at a TB centre

pathwayList.name: Breathing problem
pathwayList.asks: Breathless at rest, can they speak, sudden or gradual, wheeze, chest pain, lip colour
pathwayList.example: Breathless even at rest → S3 at once, no further questions

pathwayList.name: Chest pain
pathwayList.asks: Pressure, spread to arm or jaw, sweating, age and risk factors
pathwayList.example: Low threshold: current chest pain at 40+ or with sugar / BP → S3

pathwayList.name: Headache or dizziness
pathwayList.asks: Sudden worst-ever pain, one-sided weakness, stiff neck, head injury, fainting, BP

pathwayList.name: Abdominal pain
pathwayList.asks: Where it hurts, how it started and is changing, vomiting, fever, swelling, blood
pathwayList.example: Pain moving to the lower right, worse on walking → S3

pathwayList.name: Vomiting or loose motions
pathwayList.asks: How often, fluids kept down, urine, dehydration signs, blood, who the patient is
pathwayList.example: Vomited 10 times, can't keep water down → S2, nurse home visit

pathwayList.name: Urine problem
pathwayList.asks: Burning, how often, blood, fever with shivering, side pain, unable to pass urine
pathwayList.example: Burning urine with fever and side pain → S2, doctor today and a urine test

how.notDiagnosis: Pathways choose care and urgency only. CareCompass never names a disease.

landing.title: The right care. The right caregiver. The right time.
landing.subHi: सही देखभाल। सही देखभालकर्ता। सही समय।
landing.subEn: The right care. The right caregiver. The right time.
landing.sub: Describe the problem by voice or text, in English, Hindi or Hinglish. CareCompass checks for danger signs, decides what care fits and how urgent it is, and finds a caregiver near you, with the reason shown.
landing.stepsSub: Four steps, usually without a single follow-up question.

steps.d: Speak or type the problem, who it is for and since when.
Every message is screened for danger signs first, in three languages.
We pick the care type and urgency, and explain why in plain words.
Ranked by skill, distance, free time, language and rating. Book in one tap.

landing.careSub: Plain-language guide to what each option means.

careWhen.paramedic_home_visit: Fever or a fall at home, BP or sugar checks for someone who cannot travel.
careWhen.nurse_home_visit: Injections, drips, wound or catheter care, bedridden patients.
careWhen.gp_teleconsult: Mild, common problems that a doctor can assess on a call.
careWhen.specialist_referral: Problems lasting weeks or months, or needing a specific expert.
careWhen.emergency_referral: Danger signs: chest pain, breathing trouble, fainting, stroke signs.

landing.emTitle: In an emergency, we step aside and get you help
landing.emBody: If any danger sign is found, CareCompass skips questions and booking. It shows Call 112 and Ambulance 108 in large buttons, step-by-step instructions in your language, and your location to read out to the operator.
landing.previewSub: A few profiles from the demo network across Delhi NCR (synthetic data).

built.d: Text size control and high-contrast mode on every page.
Speak instead of typing. Answers are read aloud in Hindi or English.
Big buttons, one-tap answers like Haan / Nahi, no jargon.
Icons with every label and short sentences in the user's own language.
